name: Mule deer
fact: Western deer named for its big, mule-like ears.

name: Elk
fact: The wapiti, second-largest member of the deer family.

name: Pronghorn
fact: The fastest land mammal in the Americas, up to 55 mph.

name: Mountain cottontail
fact: A small western rabbit with black-tipped, rounded ears.

name: Jackalope
fact: A legend credited to a Douglas taxidermist. Mostly antler.

name: Chokecherry
fact: Ripe fruit is edible; the pits and leaves are poisonous.

name: Serviceberry
fact: Sweet, nutty berries long used by Indigenous peoples.

name: Prickly pear
fact: The peeled, de-seeded fruit can be eaten raw.

name: Arrowleaf balsamroot
fact: Leaves, cooked roots and seeds are edible.

name: Prairie onion
fact: Thin round leaves and a round head of cream flowers. Smells of onion.

name: Sego lily
fact: Utah's state flower, also native to Wyoming. Easy to mistake for death camas when not in bloom.

name: Cattail
fact: Cooked rhizomes and peeled young stems are edible, from clean water.

name: Death camas
fact: Very poisonous. V-folded leaves, a tall tapering spike of cream stars, no onion smell.

name: Day-old bagels
fact: Hard enough to patch a tire. Still bagels.

name: Dented cans
fact: No labels, no problem. Dinner is a surprise.

name: Pizza crusts
fact: Only the crusts. Somebody had priorities.

name: Mystery burrito
fact: It is green, it is moving, and it smells. Leave it.
